title: Monotonicity conjecture for the number of subset sizes in the Z-curve
statement:
Let $D$ and $K$ be parameters of the set $\mathbf{X}^D_K$, and let $n$ be such that $K=n+1$. A subset size is a cardinality attained by a subset of $\mathbf{X}^D_K$.

**Monotonicity conjecture.** For given values of $D$ and $K=n+1$, the minimum number of subsets of different sizes in $\mathbf{X}^D_K$ is at least equal to the number of subsets of different sizes when $K=n$.

The conjecture concerns how the possible subset-size counts change under one further subdivision of the $Z$-curve; the supplied text gives observational motivation but no proof or resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.04611

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
source_name: Diego Vazquez Gonzalez and Hsing-Kuo Pao, “The Z-Curve as an n-Dimensional Hypersphere: Properties and Analysis”, arXiv:2410.04611 (2024).
